additional_concerns: Footnote 3 is supplied and attaches to XML and PDF submissions. The extracted missing-footnote and unresolved-method-antecedent statements are stale. The web-form method has no marker 3; extending this certificate requirement to it is unsupported.

The PDF permission is supported as a method choice subject to the prescribed format and e-Cert requirement. If its extracted conditions are treated as exhaustive sufficient conditions, they omit e-Cert. This extraction issue does not establish a defect in a resubmission-trigger formula.
The XML passage separately requires prompt liaison with JFIU to arrange a technical test. The atomic schema claim does not exhaust those duties.

The date-only candidate includes filings before 9:00am on 2 February 2026. The source states both a date-effective channel rule and a 9:00am operational launch. Retain the competing interpretations of 'following its implementation'; the predicates are not equivalent.
The governing timezone and precise inclusion of the launch instant are not expressly resolved. Authoritative temporal clarification is missing, with no identifiable supplied dependency mapping.

The blackout provision permits urgent direct contact, but contact alone does not establish an STR submission. An actual submission through such contact should not be excluded merely because contact was involved. The provision does not authorize unrestricted alternative-channel filing after launch.

For a known non-submission within licensed-firm scope, node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb can return FALSE; the other event candidates return OUT_OF_SCOPE. Their assessment domains require a consistent interpretation.

FALSE under these trigger questions does not establish format, schema or certificate compliance, or permission to use another channel. Adding compliance requirements as conditions of the historical trigger would need separate support.

The history candidate delegates event existence, report identity and sufficient negative-history evidence to an external Boolean. Missing history must not become FALSE. Later resubmission does not erase a historical trigger, and automatic migration is distinct from a new submission.
Original-submitter and responsible-entity classifications may differ for delegated filings or responsibility changes. The supplied source does not establish their equivalence.
The promised JFIU resubmission guidance is absent. It may clarify procedures or disputed boundaries; its issuance is not stated as a precondition to the duty. No supplied dependency ID identifies it.

All supplied external dependency hashes are null and their authority mappings are unspecified. No AVAILABLE assessment or guessed catalogue assignment is justified. These scoped NOT_APPLICABLE findings do not authorize pruning the claims from a broader compliance model.
